transcript.text: Chick-fil-A makes more than these three
businesses combined. So, here are the
six things they do that you can apply to
your business. Number one is focus. They
focused on selling chicken sandwiches
for the past 59 years in making the
chicken sandwich better and better and
better. Number two, they built slowly.
Chick-fil-A grew slowly, didn't take on
debt, and is family-owned. Its
competitor in the early days, Boston
Market, grew as fast as it could, took
on debt, went public, and now is out of
business. Number three, values.
Chick-fil-A could increase their sales
by 13% or $650 million per year by
simply being open on Sunday. But, they
don't let money compromise their values,
which makes them more money in the long
term. Number four, hospitality. They
hired people from Ritz-Carlton to help
them create exquisite experiences at
Chick-fil-A. Number five, compounding.
They buy the land and the building for
each store they build, so over time the
real estate value continues to go up and
compound. Number six, they don't change
their menu, and this is huge. They just
get better and better at what they sell.
So, instead of being mediocre at many
things, they're exceptional at a few.
Their menu is a quarter of the size of
many other big fast food chains, and all
the stuff on there is arguably, opinion,
better. Tactics like these helped me
build my portfolio of companies that
generate over $250 million annually. You
can follow for more business breakdowns.
